sentence: Omeprazole is a proton pump inhibitor, a medicine that lowers the amount of acid the stomach makes.
note: NHS page summary: omeprazole is a PPI that reduces stomach acid.

sentence: The NHS says it is used to treat or prevent stomach ulcers, heartburn and gastro-oesophageal reflux disease, often called GORD.
note: Returned NHS text: used for heartburn, acid reflux, and to prevent and treat stomach ulcers.

sentence: It is also used, together with antibiotics, to treat a stomach infection called Helicobacter pylori.
note: Returned NHS summary lists H. pylori treatment with antibiotics.

sentence: Omeprazole comes as capsules and tablets, and the NHS says they are swallowed whole with water or squash.
note: Returned how-and-when text: tablets and capsules swallowed whole with water or squash.

sentence: Adults usually take it once a day, first thing in the morning.
note: Returned text: adults usually take it once a day, first thing in the morning.

sentence: The NHS says capsules are prescription only, while some tablets can be bought from pharmacies and supermarkets for adults.
note: Returned text: capsules prescription only; tablets sold in pharmacies and supermarkets, limited to adults.

sentence: Tablets bought this way are for short use, and the NHS advises telling a doctor if there is no improvement after the short course.
note: Returned text: pharmacy product limited to a short course; tell a doctor if no better.

sentence: Omeprazole blocks the last step in the making of stomach acid.
note: StatPearls text (via search summary): blocks the final step of acid production.

sentence: It acts on an enzyme called the proton pump, which sits on acid-making cells in the stomach wall.
note: StatPearls: inhibits H+/K+ ATPase on parietal cells.

sentence: StatPearls says the drug builds up inside these cells and binds to the enzyme in a way that cannot be undone.
note: StatPearls: concentrates in parietal cells, covalent irreversible binding.

sentence: This is why its effect lasts much longer than the drug stays in the blood.
note: StatPearls: effect outlasts roughly one-hour blood half-life.

sentence: The NHS says people may start to feel better within a few days, but it can take up to four weeks to work fully.

sentence: The effect on acid builds up over the first few days of treatment.

sentence: By lowering acid, it is widely used for indigestion, heartburn and acid reflux.

sentence: The NHS lists headache, stomach pain, feeling or being sick, constipation or diarrhoea, and passing more wind than usual as common side effects.
note: Returned side-effects page summary lists these common effects.

sentence: It says omeprazole can also cause dizziness or blurred vision, and that anyone affected should not drive, cycle or use machinery or tools until they feel better.

sentence: Serious side effects are rarer.

sentence: The NHS lists a very low level of vitamin B12, weakened bones and a serious allergic reaction called anaphylaxis.
